title: Jnana yoga: neti neti in practice; Shankara's method; the Ashtavakra Gita opening (6 of 7)
hook: a king asks for a long path; the sage says: right now
tomorrow: Jnana yoga: neti neti in practice; Shankara's method; the Ashtavakra Gita opening (7 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ashtavakra, the sage of eight bends, and King Janaka's three questions. How do I know? How am I free? How do I let go? Your line: who am I? Today, the answer. Day two hundred seventy-nine.

Most of us assume anything worth having takes a long time. Learning an instrument: years. Getting in shape: months of mornings. So when a king asks how to be free, you'd expect a long program. Twelve years in a forest. A thousand rules. A ladder with a hundred rungs. Ashtavakra's answer starts gently enough, with a little advice about how to live. And then, a few verses in, it says something so bold you may read the line twice to be sure you got it.
screen: `WORTH HAVING TAKES A LONG TIME.` → `A KING ASKS HOW TO BE FREE.` → `THEN THE ANSWER GETS BOLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the opening of Ashtavakra's reply, paraphrased. If you want freedom, my child, treat the pull of the senses like poison, and drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar. That's the gentle part. A good life, sensibly described. Then the next verse turns everything. You are not earth. You are not water, or fire, or air, or space. To be free, know yourself as the witness of all these: awareness itself. Neti neti again, in the king's own language. The old Indian list of five elements that make up everything, and the sage says: you're none of them. You're the one they appear to. Then the verse that stops people. If you set the body aside and rest in awareness, then right now, this very moment, you'll be happy, at peace, and free. Right now. Not after twelve years. Not after you've fixed your temper or your diet. Now. A little later he adds: right and wrong, pleasure and pain, belong to the mind, not to you. You're not the doer. You're not the one who enjoys the results. You were always free. Is that too easy? Teachers in the tradition say it isn't easy at all; it's simple, which is different. Nothing has to be built. But everything you keep counting as yourself has to be seen through, the way the leader by the river had to stop counting and turn around. That's why the Ashtavakra Gita is so loved on the jnana path. It doesn't give you a ladder. It points at the floor you're already standing on.
screen: `SENSES AS POISON, VIRTUES AS NECTAR.` · `YOU ARE NOT EARTH, WATER, FIRE.` · `THE WITNESS OF ALL THESE.` · `RIGHT NOW: HAPPY, AT PEACE, FREE.` · then, large: `WHO AM I?`

segments.voice: Sit, and walk Ashtavakra's list slowly. Earth: the weight of the body on the seat. Not what I am; something I notice. Water: the moisture in the mouth. Noticed. Fire: the warmth of the skin. Noticed. Air: the breath. Noticed. Space: the room around you. Noticed. Then, for a few breaths, rest as the one noticing, right now. Not later. If the mind says it's not working, that's a thought. Noticed. The bell holds the time.
Jnana yoga, in the Ashtavakra Gita's answer: you are not the elements, but the witness of them, awareness itself; rest there, and you're free now.
Your line: who am I? Today, when you're sure something has to be fixed before you can be at peace, try one breath of Ashtavakra's right now. Day two hundred seventy-nine.

howItsDone: Students of the Ashtavakra Gita often chant or read its first chapter slowly, pausing on each verse, and use its list of the five elements as a contemplation: noticing each as known, and resting as the knower.

myth: Ashtavakra tells Janaka freedom takes many lifetimes of effort
he says: rest in awareness, and right now you'll be happy, at peace and free.
the Ashtavakra Gita begins with ethical advice
it starts by urging forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth.
teachers of the text say its teaching is easy
they say simple, not easy: nothing is built, but everything must be seen through.

fork.setup: you're King Janaka. the sage names earth, water, fire, air and space, the stuff of everything. which one does he say you are?
options: none of them: you're their witness.
fork.reveal: none. you are the witness of all these, awareness itself, he says, and resting there you're free right now.

original.note: Sanskrit: sakshi, the witness; what the Ashtavakra Gita and Vedanta call pure awareness.

trapdoor: what you thought: freedom is a reward at the end of a long spiritual road.
what it means: the Ashtavakra Gita says you're already the witness, and freedom is recognizing it now.

what a scholar hears: Ashtavakra Gita 1.2–1.4 move from ethical preparation to the claim that the self is the sakshi of the five elements; 1.6 denies that the self is the doer (karta) or enjoyer (bhokta), a central Advaita point.

sources.ref: Ashtavakra Gita 1.2–1.4 (poison and nectar; not the five elements; the witness; free now)
Ashtavakra Gita 1.6 (not the doer, not the enjoyer)
